about: Basic foods (meat, poultry, fish, eggs, dairy, grains, fruit and vegetables) under the names people type. Each copies one USDA food by FDC id; the basis names it. See README.md.

foods.name: Chicken tenderloin, raw
foods.basis: USDA Foundation Foods 2646170: "Chicken, breast, boneless, skinless, raw". The chicken tenderloin (tender) is the pectoralis minor muscle on the underside of the breast. USDA has no separate analysis of unbreaded tenderloin, so this uses USDA boneless, skinless chicken breast meat. Not for breaded or fried tenders.

foods.name: Chicken tenderloin, cooked
foods.basis: USDA Foundation Foods 331960: "Chicken, broiler or fryers, breast, skinless, boneless, meat only, cooked, braised". The chicken tenderloin (tender) is the pectoralis minor muscle on the underside of the breast. USDA has no separate analysis of unbreaded tenderloin, so this uses USDA boneless, skinless chicken breast meat. Not for breaded or fried tenders. Cooked by braising (moist heat); about 100 g raw gives about 75 g cooked.

foods.name: Chicken tenderloin, grilled
foods.basis: USDA SR Legacy 171534: "Chicken, broiler or fryers, breast, skinless, boneless, meat only, cooked, grilled". The chicken tenderloin (tender) is the pectoralis minor muscle on the underside of the breast. USDA has no separate analysis of unbreaded tenderloin, so this uses USDA boneless, skinless chicken breast meat. Not for breaded or fried tenders.
